Subject: Multiparametric MRI Prostate | Maastricht UMC+ | 28 January 2025

Clinical indication: Assessing elevated prostate-specific antigen at 8.1 ng/mL alongside a previously positive biopsy, raising clinical suspicion for clinically significant prostate cancer.

FINDINGS:
The gland measures 47.0 mL in volume. An asymmetric contour highlights a focal abnormality within the right posterior peripheral zone, spanning the base to mid region. T2-weighted sequences demonstrate pronounced hypointensity, while diffusion-weighted imaging confirms marked restriction with correspondingly depressed apparent diffusion coefficient values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced imaging captures early focal uptake. The lesion spans approximately 18 x 15 x 12 mm. No extraprostatic extension, seminal vesicle invasion, suspicious pelvic lymphadenopathy, or osseous lesions are present.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion located in the right posterior peripheral zone (base/mid), measuring approximately 18 mm. Prostate volume 47.0 mL. PSA density 0.14. csPCa probability 0.82094896.

previous_notes.author: Dr. S. de Vries (GP)
previous_notes.text: Routine screening detected a prostate-specific antigen value of 8.2 ng/mL. Following an upward trajectory and the patient's history of a prior positive biopsy, a referral to the urology outpatient clinic was processed to facilitate further evaluation and potential repeat imaging. The individual reports no urinary symptoms.

previous_notes.author: Dr. S. de Vries (GP)
previous_notes.text: Serial tracking shows the prostate-specific antigen concentration increased to 6.0 ng/mL relative to the earlier measurement. A repeat testing interval was scheduled for three months out. The patient continues to address hypercholesterolaemia through his established lipid-lowering regimen.
